sections.executive_summary:
Florida splits non-medical home care into two legal lanes, and the line between them is **hands-on care**. A **companion** or **homemaker** may sit with, accompany, shop, cook and clean for a client, but Florida law says each "may not provide hands-on personal care to a client" [S1]. An organization that offers only companion and homemaker services registers with AHCA under s. 400.509, F.S. for **$50.75 per biennium** [S2][S17]. **Personal care** — help with bathing, dressing, eating, personal hygiene, transfers, walking and medications — is delivered by home health aides or CNAs, and that makes the business a **home health agency (HHA)** that needs an AHCA license [S1][S6]. The license can be limited to non-skilled services: no accreditation and no director of nursing are required, but the agency must have an RN make supervisory visits, carry **$250,000 per claim** of malpractice and of liability insurance, pay **$2,005** per biennium ($1,705 license + $300 assessment), and prove funds of at least 3 months of projected expenses [S3][S8][S12][S16]. A **nurse registry** ($2,000) is a third route, but the aides it refers are independent contractors it may not supervise [S7][S19].

Money comes mostly from **private pay**. CareScout puts Florida's median for a non-medical caregiver at **$32 an hour** [S36]. Public money is real but thin: SMMC Long-Term Care plans cover personal care, homemaker, companion and respite for 176,819 members (125,912 in the home and community-based rate group) [S23][S25], but plans negotiate rates privately; the published fee-for-service state-plan personal care rate is **$17.32** an hour [S26], but that benefit covers only recipients under 21 (Rule 59G-4.215) [S67]; adult LTC plan rates are negotiated, unpublished and may be higher or lower. Used here as an assumption, $17.32 is less than an aide costs at the new **$15.00 minimum wage** with taxes [S43]. APD's iBudget waiver pays agencies **$24.28 an hour** for Personal Supports [S29], and Area Agencies on Aging buy personal care at **$27.00–$29.92** an hour in Pasco-Pinellas [S33][S34].

The model is built at Tampa Bay wages. The **40-client non-skilled HHA, all private pay**, nets about **+$8,990 a month (9.8% margin; break-even at 61% occupancy)**. A 20-client companion-only registrant nets about +$3,328 with the owner as administrator. A 60-client agency split between private pay and AAA programs roughly breaks even (+$450). A Medicaid-LTC-only agency at the $17.32 assumption loses about $42,345 a month and needs plan rates of about **$23.20 an hour** just to break even at minimum wage; an APD-only Personal Supports agency of 30 clients loses about $3,875 a month.

The opportunity is a private-pay, licensed (non-skilled) HHA in a large retiree market — 22.8% of Floridians are 65 or older [S55] — priced near the $32 median, with public payers added only where the contracted rate covers a $15+ wage plus about 21% in burden and paid travel time.
sections.service_model:
### Who is served
Older adults and adults with disabilities who need help at home: companionship, meals, housekeeping, errands and escort (companion/homemaker), and hands-on help with activities of daily living (personal care). Florida's statute defines **personal care** as help "in the activities of daily living, such as dressing, bathing, eating, or personal hygiene," plus help with transfers, ambulation and medications as permitted by rule [S1].

### Which license do you need?
| What your caregivers do | Florida authorization | Key rules |
|---|---|---|
| Companionship, outings, meal prep, light housekeeping, shopping, medication *reminders* — **no hands-on care** | **Homemaker and Companion Services registration** (s. 400.509, F.S.; Rule 59A-8.025) | $50.75 per biennium; register before serving anyone; service area limited to counties in your health planning district; level 2 screening; no insurance minimum, no RN [S2][S13][S17] |
| Bathing, dressing, toileting, feeding, transfers, help with self-administered medication (hands-on personal care) | **Home Health Agency license**, which may be limited to **non-skilled** services (aides, CNAs, homemakers, companions) | $1,705 + $300 per biennium; $250,000/claim malpractice + liability insurance; CPA-compiled projections and contingency funds; RN supervisory visits; no accreditation or DON if non-skilled [S3][S8][S12][S15][S16] |
| Referring independent-contractor CNAs, aides, companions or homemakers to clients for a fee | **Nurse Registry license** | $2,000; workers are independent contractors the registry "may not monitor, supervise, manage, or train"; CNAs/aides only for patients under a physician's care [S7][S19] |
| Nursing or therapy (skilled care) | HHA license with skilled services | Accreditation within 120 days of application; director of nursing; 24-hour on-call [S3][S4][S15] |

Rule 59A-8.0095 lists what each worker may do: homemakers keep house, cook, do laundry and shopping and give cosmetic assistance; companions provide company and escort and keep a written service record; both may **verbally remind** a client to take medication [S12]. Anything hands-on requires an aide or CNA working for a licensed HHA (or referred by a nurse registry). An HHA's license lists the authorized services, and advertising a service that is not on the license is unlicensed activity [S6].

**Exemptions that matter:** s. 400.464(6) exempts, among others, individuals acting alone who are not affiliated with an agency or registry, and home health services delivered for state agencies (including services for people with developmental disabilities) directly or through contractors [S6]. APD contractors who provide only companion services to people with developmental disabilities are exempt from registration [S2], and the iBudget handbook lets solo or agency providers that meet its Chapter 1 qualifications deliver Personal Supports [S31] — confirm with your APD regional office before relying on this.

### Operating model
Clients are served in their own homes under a written service agreement that lists the services, private-pay rates and payment sources [S5]. Non-skilled personal care needs no physician order (s. 400.487(2) applies to skilled care) [S5]. The HHA admits clients, schedules aides, and sends an RN for supervisory visits with the client's consent and agreement to pay [S5][S12].
sections.licensing_pathway:
### Track A — Homemaker & companion registration (no hands-on care)
1. **Form the business.** File LLC Articles on Sunbiz ($100 + $25 registered agent) [S51]; get an EIN (free) [S53].
2. **Pick your service area.** Initial applications must list the counties to be served; they must be inside the health service planning district where your address of record is located [S13].
3. **Screen people.** Owners/controlling interests, the administrator/managing employee and the financial officer need AHCA level 2 screening through the Clearinghouse [S17][S56][S57].
4. **Apply.** File AHCA Form 3110-1003 with the Health Care Licensing Application Addendum (Form 3110-1024) and the **$50.75** fee to the Long Term Care Services Unit (Mail Stop 33) [S17][S18][S20]. Missing documents or fees must arrive within 21 days of an omission notice or the application is withdrawn [S17].
5. **Before you serve anyone,** registration must be issued [S13]. Put the AHCA registration number in every advertisement [S2].
6. **Renew every two years,** at least 60 days before expiration [S13].

### Track B — Home health agency, non-skilled (hands-on personal care)
1. **Form the business and get zoning sign-off.** You need proof of the legal right to occupy the office and a letter from the local government official stating that zoning is met [S15].
2. **Name the key people.** An **administrator** (Florida-licensed physician, PA or RN, or a person with 1 year of supervisory/administrative experience in home health or a licensed facility) and a written **alternate administrator** [S1][S4][S12]; a **financial officer**; and an **RN** who will make aide supervisory visits (required for non-skilled agencies) [S15][S12]. A DON is required only if you provide skilled nursing [S4][S12]. The administrator or alternate must be available to the public for 8 consecutive hours between 7 a.m. and 6 p.m. on weekdays [S11].
3. **Buy insurance:** at least **$250,000 per claim** of malpractice and of liability coverage; proof goes with the application [S3].
4. **Prepare the financials.** A CPA-compiled projected balance sheet, income and expense statement and cash-flow statement for the first 2 years (AHCA Form 3100-0009), showing assets, credit and projected revenue cover projected expenses; **no month in the first year may project an operating margin of 15% or more** [S3][S20]. Show independent evidence of funds for startup, working capital and contingency of **at least 3 months of average projected expenses** (contingency at least 1 month) through break-even [S8].
5. **Write the business plan** — how you will get patients and recruit and keep staff (signed) [S3][S15].
6. **Apply on AHCA Form 3110-1011** with the Addendum, mark "only non-skilled services" and the accreditation exemption, list counties, hours and personnel, and pay **$1,705 + $300** [S15][S16]. Non-skilled agencies are exempt from accreditation [S3][S15].
7. **Licensure survey.** AHCA surveys agencies before initial licensure, then unannounced at least every 36.9 months per the published rule text [S11]. Be open during the hours you listed; surveyors visit then [S15].
8. **Renew biennially,** reporting your patient count on the renewal application and a CEMP approval (or submission) from the last 365 days [S15].

To add nursing later, file an "Addition of Skilled Care Services" application, pay the fee again and obtain non-provisional accreditation within 120 days [S3][S15][S16].

### Track C — Nurse registry
AHCA Form 3110-7004, $2,000 fee, proof of financial ability [S19][S20]. Referred caregivers are independent contractors; the registry cannot supervise or train them [S7]. This model does not cover registries.

### Public payers (after you are licensed)
- **SMMC LTC plans:** enroll as a Florida Medicaid provider (federal rules require states to screen and enroll managed-care network providers) [S60], then credential with each LTC plan in your region [S64].
- **APD iBudget:** enroll as a waiver provider for Personal Supports and meet the handbook's staff qualifications and training [S31].
- **Area Agencies on Aging:** apply as a vendor; the Pasco-Pinellas AAA checks licensure, insurance, complaints, Clearinghouse results and references before approving [S33].

No official end-to-end processing time was found for either track (see What This Report Does Not Claim).
sections.reimbursement:
### How money flows
**Private pay (most revenue).** Families pay by the hour. CareScout's 2025 Florida median for a non-medical caregiver is **$32/hour** ($73,216 a year at 44 hours a week), up 7% from 2024; Florida ranks 39th among states [S36][S37]. The figure blends personal care and companion care, so a companion-only registrant may need to price lower.

**Medicaid — SMMC Long-Term Care plans.** Florida does not pay home care agencies from a state LTC fee schedule. Members who meet nursing-home level of care enroll in an LTC plan, which authorizes and pays personal care, homemaker, adult companion care, respite and other services [S23]. Plans set rates in their provider contracts and AHCA publishes no LTC rate table [S23][S28]. The 2022 General Appropriations Act funded rate increases so Medicaid direct-care workers earn at least $15.00 an hour and required plans to pass them through, including for LTC services that are not on a fee schedule [S28]. With the statewide minimum now $15.00 [S43], that floor no longer adds anything above the law. Florida Medicaid publishes a fee-for-service **S9122 maximum of $17.32/hour** (2026) [S26], but S9122 is the state-plan personal care rate for Medicaid recipients under 21 (Rule 59G-4.215) [S67] — it is not an adult LTC rate. Adult LTC plan rates are negotiated, are not published, and may be higher or lower. This report uses $17.32 only as a labeled assumption for plan rates. Seven plans had LTC members on 9/30/2026: Aetna, Florida Community Care, Humana, Molina, Simply, Sunshine and United [S25].

**Medicaid — APD iBudget waiver.** Personal Supports (help with ADLs, meal preparation, supervision and community access for adults) pays agencies **$6.07 per 15 minutes ($24.28/hour)** 1:1, or **$197.37 a day** when more than 8 hours a day are needed; rates took effect 7/1/2024 and are the latest APD change listed [S29][S30][S31]. Transportation and travel are built into the rate [S31].

**State and federal aging programs.** Area Agencies on Aging buy personal care, homemaker, companion and respite for Community Care for the Elderly, Home Care for the Elderly, the Alzheimer's Disease Initiative and Older Americans Act clients. In May 2026 the Pasco-Pinellas AAA approved new HHA vendors at **$27.00–$29.92/hour for personal care and respite** and **$26.00–$27.30 for homemaker and companionship** [S33][S34]. Hours are limited by funding, and each program has a wait list [S35].

### What the rates mean
At Tampa Bay's 75th-percentile aide wage ($17.42) [S38], with 4% paid non-billable time and 16% payroll burden, an aide hour costs about **$21.02**. Private pay at $32 leaves about $11 an hour for overhead; the AAA's $27.00 leaves about $6; iBudget's $24.28 leaves about $5 even at the $16.45 median wage; the $17.32 Medicaid assumption (under-21 FFS rate) is **below** the cost of an aide paid the $15.00 minimum (about $18.10 with burden). Medicaid EVV applies to personal care [S54].
sections.demand:
### Demographics
Florida had 23.46 million residents in July 2025; **22.8% are 65 or older** and 8.9% of those under 65 have a disability [S55].

### Public programs (referral pipelines)
- **SMMC Long-Term Care:** 176,819 members on 9/30/2026, of whom **125,912** were in the home and community-based rate category (living at home or in assisted living) and 50,907 in nursing facilities [S25]. Miami-Dade alone had 61,139 LTC members; Broward 13,647; Hillsborough 12,746; Palm Beach 11,755; Pinellas 8,844 [S25]. Enrollment is not an entitlement: applicants are screened by the Aging and Disability Resource Center and released from a wait list by priority score [S23][S24].
- **APD iBudget waiver:** 37,645 enrolled and **15,504 waiting in pre-enrollment** (June 1, 2026); 9,750 enrollees used Personal Supports in April 2026 [S32]. Of those in pre-enrollment categories 3–7, about 62% received neither APD nor Medicaid state plan services [S32].
- **Aging network wait lists (Pasco-Pinellas, May 1, 2026):** Homemaker 2,860; Community Care for the Elderly 2,610; Alzheimer's Disease Initiative 733; Home Care for the Elderly 483; SMMC LTC 1,958 [S35]. The AAA notes these are not unduplicated counts [S35].

### Private-pay referral sources
Hospital and rehab discharge planners, assisted living and independent living communities, elder-law attorneys and care managers, physicians' offices, and online search. No sourced referral volumes were found.
sections.operations:
### Staffing rules (non-skilled HHA)
- **Administrator** with s. 400.462(1) qualifications and a written **alternate**; one administrator may run up to five HHAs with identical controlling interests [S1][S4][S12].
- **RN supervisory visits** to patients receiving aide services, with the patient's consent and agreement to pay; frequency is "as needed" based on the patient's condition and the aide's training [S5][S12]. Agencies without skilled services must have written policies on RN supervisor availability during service hours [S11].
- **Home health aides:** before serving, documentation of at least **40 hours of training** (16 required topics, taught by or under an RN with 2 years of experience, one in home health) **or** a passed AHCA competency test (all 14 skills; 90 of 104 written questions) [S12]. Aides who assist with self-administered medication need **2 hours** of medication training [S12].
- **CNAs:** current Florida certification [S12]. Aides and CNAs keep **current CPR** and receive **annual in-service** training [S12].
- **Everyone:** a one-time HIV/AIDS course within 30 days of employment [S12]; **dementia training** — basic information at hire, a 1-hour course within 30 days for staff with client contact (free from DOEA online), and 2 more hours within 7 months [S9][S10].
- **No staffing ratios or caseload limits** are set [S4].
- **Level 2 background screening** through the Clearinghouse for employees with client contact, rescreened every 5 years [S56][S57][S15].

### Homemaker/companion registrants
No RN, no aide training standard and no insurance minimum, but: level 2 screening (attested on the application) [S17]; verification of each worker's employment history (two documented attempts satisfy "diligent effort") [S2][S13]; client records with emergency contacts, physician, service agreement, services and frequency, diet and allergies, and activity limits [S13]; and dementia training [S9].

### APD Personal Supports providers
Staff must be 18+, have a high school diploma or GED and one year of verifiable experience (or 30 college semester hours); providers keep training records for five years and complete the handbook's required training [S31].

### Labor law
Agencies are third-party employers and may not use the FLSA companionship exemption, so overtime applies [S61]; travel between clients during the day is paid time [S62]. Florida's minimum wage is **$15.00** from 9/30/2026 [S43][S44], and local governments cannot set a higher private-sector minimum [S45]. Workers' comp is mandatory at 4+ employees [S46].

### Systems
Scheduling, care notes and billing software; **electronic visit verification** for Medicaid personal care (federal requirement) [S54]; a Comprehensive Emergency Management Plan for HHAs (Rule 59A-8.027; CEMP approval or submission is required at renewal) [S14][S15].
sections.market_conditions:
### Pricing
Private-pay non-medical home care: **$32/hour** median, +7% over 2024 [S36][S37]. AAA program rates in Pasco-Pinellas: $27.00–$29.92 for personal care, $26.00–$27.30 for homemaker/companion [S33][S34]. Medicaid FFS state-plan personal care (recipients under 21) $17.32 [S26][S67]; adult LTC plan rates are negotiated and unpublished; iBudget Personal Supports $24.28/hour [S29].

### Wages
Home health and personal care aides (BLS OEWS May 2025): Florida 25th percentile **$15.16**, median **$16.25**, 75th **$17.25**; Tampa median $16.45 and 75th $17.42; Miami median $15.81; Orlando median $16.40 [S38]. Those wages were measured when the minimum was $13.00; the minimum rose to **$14.00 on 9/30/2025 and $15.00 on 9/30/2026** [S43], which pushes the bottom of the scale up and compresses the gap to the median. Registered nurses: Florida median $40.48, Tampa $41.09 [S42]. Office roles: Tampa medical secretary median $43,770; social and community service manager median $77,560 [S39][S41].

### Trends
- The 2026 minimum-wage step raised the floor under every Medicaid-funded hour while the iBudget rate has not changed since July 2024 [S29][S30][S43].
- AHCA amended the HHA licensure and personnel rules in 2026 (59A-8.003 on 1/26/2026; 59A-8.0095 on 5/31/2026) and the emergency-management, geographic-area and scope-of-service rules [S14].
- LTC enrollment grew 1.4% in one month (174,349 to 176,819) to September 2026 [S25].

No sourced count of Florida home care agencies or registrants was found.
sections.financial_narrative:
### How the model is built
Capacity is the active census the office is sized for; occupancy (90% default) is the share actually on service in a month (operator assumption). Revenue = hourly rate × billable hours. Private-pay and Medicaid clients are modeled at **80 billable hours per client-month** (about 18.5 hours a week) and AAA-program clients at 40 — operator estimates. Caregivers are paid for billable hours plus 4% non-billable time (travel between clients is paid [S62]).

- **Prices:** private pay $32/hour (CareScout Florida median) [S36]; AAA personal care $27.00 (lowest Pasco-Pinellas new-vendor rate) [S34]; SMMC LTC at $17.32 (assumption: the FFS S9122 rate, which covers recipients under 21 under Rule 59G-4.215 [S67]; adult LTC plan rates are negotiated, unpublished and may be higher or lower) [S26]; iBudget Personal Supports $6.07 per 15 minutes [S29].
- **Wages (Tampa–St. Petersburg MSA, BLS OEWS May 2025):** HHA aides $17.42 (75th percentile), companions and APD staff $16.45 (median), Medicaid-LTC aides $15.00 (minimum wage) [S38][S43]; RN $41.09 [S42]; administrator $77,560 (median) or $62,020 (25th percentile, owner-operators) [S39]; scheduler $43,770 [S41]; care coordinator $46,250 [S40].
- **Payroll burden 16%:** 9% taxes (FICA 7.65% plus FUTA and 2.7% Florida reemployment tax on the first $7,000) [S47][S48][S49][S50], 4% workers' comp and 3% benefits (operator estimates).
- **Fixed costs:** the HHA license and assessment ($2,005 ÷ 24) [S16] or the $50.75 registration [S17], LLC annual report ($138.75 ÷ 12) [S52], insurance at the $250,000/claim HHA minimum [S3], software, accounting, marketing, utilities and rent (operator estimates). Florida has no local minimum wages [S45].

### Results at 90% occupancy
| Configuration | Monthly net | Margin | Break-even occupancy |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-skilled HHA, 40 clients, private pay (default) | +$8,990 | 9.8% | 61% |
| Homemaker/companion registrant, 20 clients, private pay (owner-administrator at $62,020) | +$3,328 | 7.2% | 71% |
| Non-skilled HHA, 60 clients, 50% private / 50% AAA programs | +$450 | 0.5% | 88% |
| APD iBudget Personal Supports, 30 clients (owner-administrator) | −$3,875 | -7.4% | not reachable (≈41 clients) |
| Non-skilled HHA, 100 clients, SMMC LTC only at $17.32 | −$42,345 | -34.0% | not reachable at any census |

At the conservative 80% census the 40-client HHA still nets about +$5,930 a month and the 20-client registrant +$1,583; the mixed agency loses $2,338.

### Why Medicaid-only loses money
At $17.32 an hour, an aide paid the $15.00 minimum costs about $18.10 with 4% paid travel time and 16% burden — before supervision, software or rent. Each client loses about $137 a month before any fixed cost, so no census fixes it. The 100-client LTC agency breaks even only if its plan rate is about **$23.20/hour** at the minimum wage, or **$26.10/hour** at Tampa's 75th-percentile aide wage. Get the plan's actual rate in writing before you build around LTC referrals. The iBudget rate ($24.28) is better, but at the $16.45 median wage a 30-client agency still loses money; it breaks even only with an aide wage of about $14.96 — below the legal minimum — or at about 41 clients with the same office (60 clients: about +$3,672 a month).

### Cash needed
For the 40-client HHA the modeled ramp-up (2 clients, adding 3 a month) reaches profit in month 10 with a cumulative operating deficit of about $80,000. AHCA separately requires evidence of funds for startup, working capital and contingency of at least 3 months of average projected expenses — about $145,000 for this configuration in year 1 [S8].

### Sensitivity (operator estimates — verify locally)
- **Private price $28 instead of $32:** the 40-client HHA loses about $2,530 a month; the 20-client registrant loses about $2,432. Break-even prices are about **$28.90** (HHA 40) and **$29.70** (registrant 20). At the AAA companion rate of $27.30, the registrant loses about $3,440.
- **60 billable hours per client-month instead of 80:** HHA 40 nets about +$1,082; the registrant loses about $1,048.
- **Aide wage $18.50 instead of $17.42:** HHA 40 nets about +$5,238; the mixed agency loses about $3,771.
- **AAA rate $29.92 instead of $27.00:** the mixed agency nets about +$3,604.

The result is most sensitive to price and to hours sold per client; small agencies live on the spread between a ~$32 private rate and a $15–17.50 wage.
sections.risks:
1. **Doing hands-on care on a companion registration.** Companions and homemakers may not provide hands-on personal care [S1]; delivering home health services without an HHA license is unlicensed activity, a misdemeanor for each day after notice, and a deceptive trade practice [S6].
2. **Medicaid rates below cost.** The published FFS state-plan personal care rate ($17.32, recipients under 21 only) is below the burdened cost of a minimum-wage aide [S26][S67][S43]; adult LTC plan rates are private, must be negotiated, and may be higher or lower.
3. **Minimum-wage compression.** The $15.00 minimum (9/30/2026) is close to the 2025 aide median ($16.25) [S38][S43]; recruiting trained aides may need $17–18.50 an hour, which cuts the private-pay margin (see sensitivity).
4. **Capital requirements.** HHAs must evidence 3 months of projected expenses and CPA-compiled projections before licensure [S3][S8].
5. **Insurance cost.** $250,000 per claim malpractice and liability is mandatory for HHAs [S3]; premiums are not public.
6. **Overtime and travel time.** The FLSA companionship exemption is unavailable to agencies, and travel between clients is paid [S61][S62].
7. **Rule changes.** AHCA amended the HHA licensure and personnel rules in 2026 [S14]; check current text before writing policies.
8. **APD rate freeze.** iBudget rates have not changed since 7/1/2024 [S29][S30] while wages rose.
9. **Background screening disqualifications** narrow the hiring pool; every client-contact employee needs level 2 screening [S56].
10. **Service-area limits.** Homemaker/companion registrants may serve only counties in their health planning district [S13]; an HHA office outside its planning district needs a separate license [S6].
sections.recommendations:
1. **Get the HHA license, limited to non-skilled services, unless you will truly never touch a client.** Most families eventually need bathing and toileting help; a companion-only registrant has to turn them away [S1]. The non-skilled HHA avoids accreditation and a DON [S3][S12].
2. **Lead with private pay at about $32 an hour** [S36] and do not discount below about $29 (the 40-client break-even). Sell 4-hour minimum shifts to protect billable hours per client.
3. **Pay aides about $17–17.50** (Tampa 75th percentile) [S38] and budget 16% burden plus paid travel time [S62].
4. **Size the office to about 40 clients** with one administrator, a part-time RN for supervisory visits and one scheduler; the default model nets about +$8,990 a month at 90% census.
5. **Raise the cash before applying:** AHCA wants evidence of about 3 months of projected expenses (≈$145,000 modeled) and CPA-compiled projections [S3][S8].
6. **Add AAA vendor agreements** where the rate is $27–30 an hour [S33][S34] to fill aide schedules, but cap them so private pay stays at least half your hours.
7. **Treat SMMC LTC plans with caution.** Ask each plan for its personal care, homemaker and companion rates; accept only if the rate covers about $23+ an hour at minimum wage (about $26 at a $17.42 wage).
8. **APD Personal Supports** works as an add-on line for an existing office, not as a stand-alone 30-client business at $24.28 an hour [S29].
9. **Start as a registrant only if capital is the constraint** — it costs $50.75 and no insurance minimum [S17], and the owner-operated 20-client model nets about +$3,328 a month — then convert to an HHA once you have the reserve.

checklist.instructions: AHCA surveys before initial licensure, then unannounced (at least every 36.9 months per the published rule). Have personnel files, training, screening, policies and service agreements ready.

checklist.task: Be open during the hours on your application
checklist.instructions: Surveyors inspect during the business hours you submitted; being closed can lead to a fine or denial.

checklist.task: Do not serve anyone until the license or registration is issued
checklist.instructions: Registration is required before providing homemaker/companion services; operating an unlicensed HHA is unlawful.

checklist.instructions: Fines start at $100 ($500 for repeats) for HHAs and homemaker/companion registrants.

checklist.instructions: Florida median $32/hour; the 40-client model breaks even at about $28.90. Build referral relationships with discharge planners, senior living, elder-law attorneys and care managers.

checklist.instructions: Protects billable hours; rates and payment sources must be in the agreement.

checklist.instructions: Registration renewals at least 60 days before expiration; late HHA renewals incur a late fee. HHA renewals report patient count and CEMP status.

corrections_vs_previous: Old checklist told applicants to prepare a '$50 registration fee'. AHCA charges $50.75 per biennium (the $50 statutory fee, CPI-adjusted), plus $25 for changes (AHCA Form 3110-1003 and checklist 3110-1003CL).
Old checklist linked to a 'DRAFT' PDF of Form 3110-1003 (content/download/25365). The current form is the July 2024 Word version on AHCA's HQA Applications for Licensure page.

Old checklist cited s. 400.509(8) for showing the registration number in ads and s. 400.509(4,6) for registration. Section 400.509 has seven subsections; the advertising rule is s. 400.509(5), the fee is in (3), employment-history verification in (4).

Old checklist cited 's. 400.462(16,18)' for the hands-on care prohibition. The companion and homemaker definitions (each stating they 'may not provide hands-on personal care') are s. 400.462(8) and (22); personal care is (27) and home health aide is (17).

Old checklist made dementia training conditional ('if serving ADRD clients', citing ALF statute s. 400.6045). Section 430.5025, F.S. requires every companion/homemaker provider's staff to get basic information at hire, a 1-hour course within 30 days and 2 more hours within 7 months, regardless of clientele.

Old checklist never said which license is needed for hands-on personal care and offered no path for it. Hands-on personal care is home health aide work requiring an HHA license (non-skilled is enough: no accreditation, no DON, but RN supervisory visits, $250,000/claim insurance, $2,005 fees and 3 months of funds) or a nurse registry license (ss. 400.462, 400.471, 400.506, 408.8065).
Old checklist omitted the registrant's geographic limit: service areas must be counties within the health planning district of the address of record (Rule 59A-8.025).

Old checklist asserted 'online submissions are required as of September 2024; paper applications may be rejected' and a '60–90 day' approval time. AHCA's current checklist still gives a mailing address (Mail Stop 33) and online filing for renewals/changes; no official processing time was found.

Old checklist listed 'collect employment agreements for existing staff' and 'list employees with SSNs' as application attachments. The current Form 3110-1003 asks for controlling interests, the administrator and the financial officer, with an attestation that all required staff passed level 2 screening.

Old bundle had no reimbursement or P&L analysis. Florida LTC Medicaid pays through SMMC plans at negotiated (non-public) rates; the published FFS state-plan personal care rate is $17.32/hour (S9122, 2026; covers recipients under 21 only, so it is used only as an assumption for adult LTC), below the burdened cost of a $15.00 minimum-wage aide; APD iBudget Personal Supports pays $6.07 per 15 minutes; private pay median is $32/hour.
